evidence: An X-ray reﬂectivity (XRR) curve recorded using synchrotron radiation (Fig. 1) reveals a periodic oscillation stemming from a homogeneous single ﬁlm of 138 nm thickness on the substrate. Structural information is obtained by diffraction of the X-ray beam in grazing incidence geometry (GIXRD), (Fig. 2a). The SEM images in top view b, c) reveal the presence of pinholes in the deposited ﬁlm, which becomes discontinuous upon annealing, with the formation of discrete clusters. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM), reveals two new layers (Fig. 4a). The identity of the layers is conﬁrmed in a composition proﬁle determined by EDX spectroscopy. Magnetic measurements were taken on a SQUID magnetometer MPMS-XL from QuantumDesign.
